speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is causing this, can you tell me if your stools are very loose, greasy, or foul-smelling?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby appears to be in significant pain when the abdomen is touched. Has he been vomiting, and if so, is it green or yellow (bilious)?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The absence of fever, vomiting, and diarrhea is helpful. Given the pain on palpation and distension without infection signs, have you noticed any "currant jelly" stools or episodes of the baby drawing up their legs in severe pain?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

The progression to visible abdominal swelling, decreased feeding, and abnormal stool passage in an 8-month-old with severe abdominal pain is highly suggestive of intussusception. This is a medical emergency that requires immediate reduction.
